summary: This tornado occurred with many other tornadoes on January 13, 2024. This tornado started in western Rappahannock County, and quickly moved southeast. The tornado then crossed the Rappahannock River and tore through the northeastern parts of Henrico City. The tornado then continued southeast and dissipated in Halifax County. The tornado was embedded in a squall line, and was fast-moving, so it was hard to track.

This tornado occurred with many other tornadoes on January 13, 2024. This was a relatively quick moving tornado which only caused damage on the road in between George City and Martinsville. This tornado was not warned, due to it being embedded in a squall line and unable to be detected quick enough.
This was one of 4 tornadoes that happened on January 13, 2024. This was the second strongest tornado of the day, and achieved this when it passed over a road in SE Montgomery County.
A brief tornado caused minor damage in Lake and Syracuse counties.
A waterspout came ashore in Midland County, causing minor damage.

This high-end EF4 wedge tornado, almost classified as EF5, developed in rural Autauga County, Florence, before traveling east and entering Tunkhannock County and rapidly intensifying. The tornado entered northern Spotsylvania, and caused EF4+ damage in northern Spotsylvania before crossing into Susquehanna County and causing EF4 damage in James City. The tornado then rapidly weakened and lifted in Pittsylvania County. The tornado killed 3 and injured 5.

This long-tracked, EF5 wedge tornado developed southwest of Lawport City, and intensified quickly, causing EF5 damage as soon as it entered Lawport City, Fictonia. The tornado then continued northeast over mainly rural areas before crossing the Fictonia Lake into Allegheny County, Florence. The tornado continued through much of Allegheny County before dissipating in the northeastern part of the county. The tornado killed 37 and injured 85.
A weak tornado caused one injury and minor daamge along the Tulpehocken River in Greene and Mahantango counties.
An EF1 tornado caused significant tree damage along the Greene County/Luke County border.

A violent tornado caused significant damage across Aqualand and Iredale. This long-tracked tornado started in southwestern Floyd County, causing significant damage to forests. The tornado continued east through rural Floyd, Union, and Dare counties before entering Conneaut County, Aqualand. The tornado carved directly through the town of Sundansbury, causing 3 deaths and at least 20 injuries. The tornado dissipated on the Pymatuning River east of town.

The first tornado of the day touched down 2 miles southwest of the town of Windom, in Winchester County, Florence. Unfortunately for the residents of the town, it was moving directly towards them. At 5:30pm, the tornado went straight through the town at EF4 intensity, causing significant damage, and killing one person. The tornado continued northeast through rural areas of Cambria, Montgomery, Rockingham, and Halifax counties before dissipating.

A violent tornado caused significant damage throughout Iredale and Valencia. This extremely long-tracked tornado, crossing over 100 miles, started in Northumberland County, VA, and moved northeast. The tornado moved through rural Potter and Tioga counties before crossing into Iredale. The tornado moved directly through the town of Moshannon, causing almost EF5 level damage.
A tornado caused tree damage in southwestern Iredale. No structure damage, injuries, or fatalities were reported.

An extremely violent tornado obliterated the city of Vernontown in southwestern Seyounby-Sy County. This tornado started in southeastern Eastman County, causing little damage. Almost all of the damage was observed within Vernontown. This tornado was likely EF5 for a long time, but damage of this magnitude was only observed within the city limits of Vernontown. Otherwise, tens of thousands of trees were debarked in Seyounby-Sy County.
A QLCS tornado produced minor damage throughout Itasca County.
A QLCS tornado caused minor damage across the Iredale/Orbisonia border.

An extremely violent tornado caused total destruction across northern Grandlandia. The tornado touched down in southeastern Westhampton County and moved east, directly into Lenapehanna, then downtown Mountainview, and then Albany. This tornado was one of the most violent ever seen.
An EF1 tornado caused minor damage in southwestern Grandlandia.
